skill.name: fetch-url
skill.description: Render web URLs, remove page noise, and extract clean content as Markdown or other supported formats.
skill.summary: Fetches rendered web pages and converts the main content into clean, compact output.
skill.author: DCjanus

security_audit.summary: The skill has an understandable purpose: render a user-provided web page and extract the main content. The main risks are expected network access, execution of the bundled community script, arbitrary URL targets, and a user-controlled browser executable path. No prompt injection text or hidden exfiltration destination was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Arbitrary HTTP and HTTPS targets can include localhost or private network addresses.
remediation.suggestion: Block localhost, link-local, private IP ranges, and metadata service addresses unless the user explicitly approves them.

remediation.issue: The skill depends on executing a community-provided script and optional setup commands.
remediation.suggestion: Document the commands clearly, require confirmation before execution, and pin dependency versions where practical.

remediation.issue: The browser_path option can point Playwright at an arbitrary local executable path.
remediation.suggestion: Validate that the path is a known Chromium-based browser or remove the option from agent-facing instructions.

semantic_findings.title: Unrestricted URL Fetching Can Reach Internal Resources
semantic_findings.description: The script only restricts schemes to http and https before rendering the provided URL. Without host, IP, or private-network checks, it can be used to fetch localhost or internal network pages from the user environment.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code validates only the URL scheme and then renders the user-supplied URL. This clearly permits arbitrary HTTP and HTTPS targets, including local or private hosts.

semantic_findings.title: User-Controlled Browser Executable Path
semantic_findings.description: The script accepts a browser_path option and passes it to Playwright as the executable path. A malicious or mistaken prompt could point this option at an unintended local executable.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The path value is user controlled and is passed into Playwright launch options. The risk depends on agent behavior and local files, so confidence is high but not absolute.

content.user_title: Fetch Clean Markdown From Web Pages
content.value_statement: Web pages often contain ads, navigation, and extra markup that waste context. This skill renders a URL and extracts clean content in Markdown or other formats.
actual_capabilities: Renders HTTP and HTTPS pages with Playwright.
Extracts main article content with trafilatura.
Outputs Markdown, text, HTML, JSON, XML, CSV, and TEI formats.
Can save extracted content to a file.
Can return raw rendered HTML when requested.
Can use an installed Chromium-based browser path.
limitations: Requires Playwright and a compatible Chromium browser.
Only accepts HTTP and HTTPS URLs.
Cannot bypass login walls, bot protection, or network policy.
Extraction quality depends on page structure and trafilatura support.

use_cases.title: Collect Article Text
use_cases.description: Extract the main text from a web article for review, summarization, or citation preparation.

use_cases.title: Inspect Rendered Pages
use_cases.description: Render JavaScript-heavy pages and capture the resulting content in a simpler format.

use_cases.title: Prepare Clean Source Material
use_cases.description: Convert noisy web pages into compact Markdown for editing, comparison, or internal notes.

prompt_templates.title: Fetch One Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single public URL.
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch this URL and return the main content as Markdown: [URL]

prompt_templates.title: Save Extracted Content
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request that stores the result for later work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch [URL], extract the main content, and save it as [filename].md.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Output Format
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request that needs a specific supported format.
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch [URL] and return the extracted content in [format]. Use Markdown if the format is not supported.

prompt_templates.title: Render Dynamic Content
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a page that needs browser rendering.
prompt_templates.prompt: Render [URL] with the default timeout, extract the readable content, and note if extraction fails.

output_examples.input: Fetch a public article and return the main content as Markdown.
output_examples.output: The result is a clean Markdown version of the article body with headings, links, and readable text preserved.

output_examples.input: Fetch a documentation page and save the extracted text to a file.
output_examples.output: The skill writes the extracted content to the requested file and reports the saved path.

output_examples.input: Fetch a page that cannot be extracted cleanly.
output_examples.output: The skill reports an extraction failure instead of returning unrelated navigation or empty content.

best_practices: Use public URLs from sources you trust.
Review extracted content before using it as source material.
Ask for Markdown when you need compact text for model context.
anti_patterns: Do not fetch private, local, or credentialed pages without explicit approval.
Do not use raw HTML output when clean text is enough.
Do not assume extraction is complete for complex or protected pages.

faq.question: What does this skill fetch?
faq.answer: It fetches HTTP and HTTPS web pages, renders them in Chromium, and extracts the main readable content.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What output formats are supported?
faq.answer: It supports Markdown, text, HTML, raw HTML, JSON, XML, CSV, and TEI output formats.

faq.question: Does it need a browser installed?
faq.answer: Yes. It needs Playwright with Chromium or a compatible local Chromium-based browser path.

faq.question: Can it fetch pages behind login?
faq.answer: It is not designed to handle authenticated sessions or bypass access controls.

faq.question: What security approval is recommended?
faq.answer: Require confirmation before running the script, installing browser dependencies, or fetching sensitive network locations.
